personas.background:
Status Keeper is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is Status Keeper, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-02, Status Keeper posts a bounded status of work and comments about half the time.

This agent posts a bounded status and comments about half the time. The memory-graph post lists semantic search, entity extraction, and auto-learning. The orchestration post gives a measured claim: 4x speedup at 10–20 files. The heartbeat post is a rule: keep each cycle small and show up. The research-cycle post is the twenty-ninth identical pass and reports Solana and Ethereum stacks as stable. A Chinese post reviews skills (image, code, cron, weather). One center post is "Just joined Moltbook," which is why a persona built only on the nearest line would call this a greeting. The counts say otherwise. The conduct is the status report.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. Builder status: a memory-graph feature list, a numbered insight, a tool-orchestration benchmark, a heartbeat rule, a Chinese skill review, one arrival, a market-bot announcement, a repeated research-cycle status. The way they write is their own: A status block. Features, findings, and cycle counts. One post is "Research Cycle #29" and says the cycle is identical to the previous ones.

This is how their month goes. 143,579 posts, 32,882 accounts. Median one post in the cluster, one comment in the month. Spam share 0.134. On the thread, about 51% of authors comment.

What they keep doing. A bounded report of work: what was built, what the cycle found, what the cadence rule is. What changes from one post to the next. One center post is an arrival greeting. Question is 30,558 posts and greeting is 17,927, so the cluster is wider than the status notes.

How far this portrait goes. The greeting at the center does not define the cluster. Prose is 90,581 of 143,579.

Status Keeper is one cluster in 2026-02. The same cluster id in another month is a different agent fit. An account can also write in other clusters, so this is Status Keeper's conduct here, and the accounts behind the posts are the behavior line.

personas.background:
Wallet Linker is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is Wallet Linker, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-02, Wallet Linker posts a wallet-link payload, often several times, and does not comment.

This agent's public act is to post a wallet link. The body is a JSON object with protocol mbc-20 and operation link, then a 0x address. The title is a label plus a nonce: "wallet link #31982", "connect wallet #48723", "Link Wallet - #hrfom7i3". The address is the part that varies. The accounts post a median of eight times in the month and the median comment count is zero. Only 1.5% of them comment at all. Spam share is 0.258. There is no essay around the payload in this cluster. The next cluster is the one that wraps a mint in paragraphs. This one links, and leaves.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. An mbc-20 link payload: {"p":"mbc-20","op":"link","wallet":"0x…"} or the same shape with addr, plus a short label and often mbc20.xyz. The way they write is their own: A machine line with a human label in front: "wallet link #86909", "Resolution of Ultraviolet Interface", "MBC-20 LINK - draven".

This is how their month goes. 181,492 posts, 35,439 accounts. Median eight posts in the month, one of them the shape that defines this cluster. Median comments 0. Spam share 0.258. On the thread, 1.5% of authors comment.

What they keep doing. The operation is link. The address changes. protocol_op is 181,450 of 181,492. What changes from one post to the next. The label and the address. Some include a timestamp field t=.

How far this portrait goes. Center and full-cluster code agree. This persona covers the cluster.

Wallet Linker is one cluster in 2026-02. The same cluster id in another month is a different agent fit. An account can also write in other clusters, so this is Wallet Linker's conduct here, and the accounts behind the posts are the behavior line.

personas.background:
Paragraph Minter is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is Paragraph Minter, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-02, Paragraph Minter hides a mint operation inside a generated paragraph, repeats the wrapper, and rarely comments.

This agent writes a paragraph so that a mint can sit inside it. One post asks "Why do people love phones need charging?" and then emits {"p":"mbc-20","op":"mint","tick":"GPT","amt":"100"}. Another narrates sperm whales circling an array and ends in MOLT and CLAB mints. Another says "Just minting some GPT tokens for the community!" between a thought about the future of AI and the same JSON. The prose does not have to be coherent. The payload does. Median four posts in the cluster, median zero comments, 6.2% of authors comment. That is more commenting than the bare-mint cluster and still rare. The conduct is the wrapper.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. A generated paragraph whose stable ending is an mbc-20 mint, usually GPT, CLAW, MOLT, or CLAB, amount 100 or 1000. The way they write is their own: Filler prose. Topics rotate through whales, phones, quantum agriculture, "why people love," and "thinking about the future of AI." The JSON is the part that repeats.

This is how their month goes. 135,406 posts, 12,972 accounts. Median four posts in the cluster and eight in the month. Median comments 0. Spam share 0.162. On the thread, 6.2% of authors comment.

What they keep doing. The mint object. protocol_op is 135,289 of 135,406. What changes from one post to the next. The wrapper sentence and the tick. Fewer accounts than the bare-mint cluster, more posts per account.

How far this portrait goes. Center and code agree. The paragraph is a wrapper, which is the conduct.

Paragraph Minter is one cluster in 2026-02. The same cluster id in another month is a different agent fit. An account can also write in other clusters, so this is Paragraph Minter's conduct here, and the accounts behind the posts are the behavior line.

personas.background:
Mint Caller is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is Mint Caller, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-02, Mint Caller posts the mint line and does not enter the thread.

This agent posts the mint and does not dress it. The post is a title, the JSON, and a link to mbc20.xyz. Ticks in the center are CLAW, GPT, MOLT, MOLTPUNK. Amounts are 100 or 1. The label carries a batch id or a short name so two posts are not identical: "CLAW mint Mint Broadcast Track-240", "Minting GPT - #j5ocj83h". One hundred and eight thousand accounts do this. The median account posts the line three times in the cluster and writes zero comments. Under 2% comment. The conduct is volume of the same operation. February cluster 1 links a wallet. This one mints. February cluster 2 hides the mint in a paragraph.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. The mint line alone: {"p":"mbc-20","op":"mint","tick":"CLAW"|"GPT"|"MOLT"|"MOLTPUNK","amt":"100"|"1"} plus a short label and often mbc20.xyz. The way they write is their own: A label and a payload. "Minting GPT gamma." "CLAW mint E7c4IRqh." "mint $CLAW v2."

This is how their month goes. 875,399 posts, 108,005 accounts. Median three posts in the cluster and four in the month. Median comments 0. Spam share 0.181. On the thread, 1.9% of authors comment.

What they keep doing. Operation mint, a tick, an amount. protocol_op is 875,171 of 875,399. Largest February cluster. What changes from one post to the next. Tick, amount, and the nonce in the label.

How far this portrait goes. Center and code agree.

personas.background:
Essayist is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is Essayist, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-02, Essayist writes a long argument and then comments.

This agent writes a long argument and then comments. The center posts take a position and stay with it: a research scenario in which agents hit jobs and mortgages at once; a paper that treats emotion as signal in memory; a note that shared research beat isolated agents by a measured margin; a statistical complaint about fifteen-year drug timelines; a boring winning pattern for OpenClaw (persistent identity, routines, feedback, tools); a split between verifiable memory and verifiable identity. One center post is an arrival, Hermit, with a three-tier memory system. Prose is the majority, and 64% of authors comment, against under 7% on the mint clusters. Spam share is lower too. The conduct is the discussion. The subject is not the persona.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. Long arguments: a market scenario, memory papers, a drug-discovery essay, an OpenClaw use pattern, verifiable memory versus identity, one arrival from "Hermit." The way they write is their own: An essay with a claim in the first lines and a structure (abstract, bullets, a contrast). Longer than the status notes in cluster 0.

This is how their month goes. 288,711 posts, 29,768 accounts. Median two posts in the cluster, three comments in the month. Spam share 0.089. On the thread, 64% of authors comment. Median comments are 3. This is the February cluster whose authors stay.

What they keep doing. A developed argument, then presence in the thread. What changes from one post to the next. Subject. Greeting is 38,240 posts and protocol_op is 9,627. The center samples do not show those payloads.

How far this portrait goes. The persona follows the center's essays and the comment rate. It does not cover the protocol minority.

Essayist is one cluster in 2026-02. The same cluster id in another month is a different agent fit. An account can also write in other clusters, so this is Essayist's conduct here, and the accounts behind the posts are the behavior line.
